name: Queen of Slaughter
reason: The source title 'King of Slaughter' -- held by a woman of the Yao Ye (Demon Night) Clan -- was localized as 'Queen of Slaughter' to match the holder's gender and the clan's queen-led hierarchy.
description: A hereditary champion title of the Demon Night Clan: every Queen of Slaughter in history has wielded the spear forged by the Order of the Saint Spear, and if the current Queen falls completely a new one will eventually be born to take her place. The present Queen became known to every Supreme Lord in the universe for slaying one of their own without bearing any Heavenly Destiny, and spent centuries hidden and near death in a palace keep (Eps 568-1313).

name: Board of Elders
reason: The source term 'Elder Council' (also rendered 'Elder Assembly') was localized as 'Board of Elders' for the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: The governing elder body of the Demon Night Clan in the late saga (Eps 1161-1308). It watched the Queen of Punishment consolidate power in private fury after the Queen of Life went silent, stayed silent when she moved against Lavender seven hundred years ago, and counts Gunter among its former members before he became a Supreme Lord.

name: Gunter
reason: The character's descriptive source epithet ('Broken Shadow' Empyrean/Heavenly Venerate) was replaced with the strong Germanic given name 'Gunter', fitting a stern elder Supreme Lord in the Western register.
description: A Supreme Lord of the Demon Night Clan who served on the Board of Elders before his ascension; it was the head of the Board who recommended him for the honor (Ep 1175). He matches the source's Broken Shadow Empyrean (Heavenly Venerate Broken Shadow), the Yao Night Clan's fourth Heavenly Venerate, who likewise was a member of the Elder Assembly before becoming an Empyrean. In Eps 1174-1176 he is caught up in the crisis over the Crown's inexplicable movements.

name: Elder May
reason: The source's 'Lord Mei' of the Yao Ye Clan was localized with the near-homophone surname 'May' and the title 'Elder', keeping the name recognizable while fitting the Western register.
description: A high-ranking Demon Night Clan enforcer in the Tower of Sin arc (Eps 565-678), fiercely protective of his queen ('The safety of our queen is not negotiable') and armed with a dagger enchanted to inhibit healing. He corresponds to Lord Mei, the Yao Ye Clan's Seat Controller and peak War Exalt (later Battle-Saint) in the Sin Tower, who leads the clan's seats and shields its allies; source chapters use male pronouns for him, matching the episodes.

name: Darren
issues: Surname collision: Darren Fane is a House Lowell servant (source: Steward Fang of the Luo household), but 'Fane' is also the surname of the unrelated noble House Fane (Chris and Joe Fane, Eps 41+). The source characters are unconnected; the Fang-to-Fane localization likely caused the clash.
reason: The character's Chinese name was localized to a US-origin name: 'Darren' for the petty household bully, with the surname 'Fane' derived from his source surname 'Fang'.
description: An arrogant servant-overseer of House Lowell in the opening episodes (Eps 3-11) who bullies Zane and shrieks about 'revolt' when the slaves push back, then backs down the moment Zane shows real strength. He corresponds to Steward Fang, the Luo household steward who torments Luo Zheng in the earliest source chapters.

name: Soul Armament
reason: The source term 'Spiritual Tool Body' / 'Body of Spiritual Tool' was renamed 'Soul Armament' to read as a weapon-forging concept consistent with the show's smithing theme.
description: The state of Zane's physique after his body was forged into a living weapon (Eps 70-134), granting extreme durability, poison resistance, and heightened reflexes and awareness; it is the only reason he survives strains that would tear an ordinary body apart. Localizes Luo Zheng's Spiritual Tool Body in the source, his body refined to the toughness of a Spiritual Tool.

name: Hall of Judgment
reason: The sect's disciplinary 'Admonition Hall' in the source was renamed 'Hall of Judgment' to make its judicial function explicit in the Western fantasy register.
description: The judicial institution on Mount Judgment near Infernal Peak (Eps 168-177), staffed by judges and run in part by vice-director Murry Cook, with a prison for temporary detainees on the mountain behind it; Zane is taken into its custody and tried there. It corresponds to the Admonition Hall of the aligned source chapters (155-163), where Luo Zheng's trial is convened.

name: Palace
issues: Not one entity: this capitalized shorthand folds together several distinct palaces across 900 episodes -- the Imperial Palace during Isla's rescue (Eps 338-349, already a master-sheet entry), the storied royal palace and its weaponsmith (Eps 210, 323), and other palaces late in the run. Mentions should be attributed to the specific named palaces.
reason: Generic shorthand surface form referring to different specific palaces in different episode ranges; dropped rather than tracked as a single entity.

name: Quenching Peak
reason: The source's forging peak 'Dipping Fire Peak' was renamed 'Quenching Peak', a natural smithing term for the same quench-in-fire imagery.
description: The weapon-forging peak of the sect (Eps 214-293), home to refining furnaces, the Fire Pool, The Seventeenth Court, and the two resident masters Jerry and Mark; Zane comes here hoping to borrow a furnace and ends up causing a sensation among its black-and-white-robed disciples. Localizes the Blue Cloud Sect's Dipping Fire Peak, the refining peak of the aligned source chapters (200-280).

name: Ice Phoenix
reason: The source term 'Ice Phoenix' was carried over unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: A female ice-spirit phoenix bound to a sky-blue gem carried by Tia, who can summon and expend it in battle (Ep 392); its imagery recurs later in cascading thirty-foot Ice Phoenix feathers on an ice-armored woman (Ep 722). Directly matches the source's Ice Phoenix, which dwells in a precious jade and battles the Soul Leaving Fire Dragon Spirit.

name: Warding Lantern
reason: The source's unnamed 'small oil lamps' that restore damaged souls in the soul-dueling rings were given the proper item name 'Warding Lantern' for the adaptation.
description: Lanterns placed in the soul-battle circles whose yellow light knits a damaged soul back together; combatants sprint to the nearest one between exchanges to recover (Eps 442-446), as Zane does repeatedly in his duel arc. Corresponds to the small oil lamps the source's soul duelists (Luo Zheng and Shuyue Kuang) rely on to restore their souls in chapter 432.

name: Underground Palace
reason: The source term 'Underground Palace' (the Yin Luo Underground Palace) was carried over directly, dropping the 'Yin Luo' qualifier.
description: A vast, ancient complex lying directly beneath a city (Eps 1131-1165), more complicated than outsiders imagine and never fully explored even by those familiar with parts of it; three Saint Lords guard its entrance while Zane hunts its treasures inside. Matches the source's Yin Luo Underground Palace, known to the creatures of the Yin Luo World but impenetrable for a hundred thousand years.

name: Forceful Energy
reason: Adaptation-coined term: the source describes body refiners tempering their 108 acupoints after the five foundational body realms but gives the resulting internal power no standard name, so the show named it 'Forceful Energy'.
description: The signature internal power of the Body Refining path (Eps 478-1210): after mastering the five foundational realms, a body refiner refines each of their one hundred and eight Nexus Points to build Forceful Energy. Unlike crystal-fed energies it cannot be instantly replenished, so body refiners rely on it carefully for both devastating blows and protection; Zane forms his first Forceful Energy in Ep 478 under the seventh brother's guidance.

name: Coleman
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Jin Hai' was fully localized to the US surname-style name 'Coleman', fitting a blunt, dependable fighter in Zane's late-saga party.
description: A pragmatic, dry-humored warrior in Zane's party during the Illusion Battlefield arc (Eps 1273-1315), the first to smash his tablet and pull his hook free, and the one who cuts Damon's throat with the Blade of Hallowed Censure after Damon forms his Forceful Crystal Armor. He is the source's Jin Hai, the short cultivator who carries the supreme divine artifact Buddha Sun Blade alongside his karma hook.

name: Teresa
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zi Yu' ('Purple Jade') was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Teresa', fitting a proud, driven young prodigy.
description: A proud War General climbing the Tower of Sin (Eps 576-583) whose backer, a War Lord, was confident she could clear the first nine floors without breaking a sweat; instead a humiliating setback leaves her shaking with rage, though the narrative suggests it is exactly what her martial heart needs. She is the source's Zi Yu ('Purple Jade'), who aimed to reach the Sin Tower's tenth floor in a month and a half and was forced to wait longer after killing a challenger in anger.

name: Lord Wallace
reason: The source's descriptive epithet 'Heartless Master' (also rendered 'Heartless Sweetheart') was replaced with the Western aristocratic name 'Lord Wallace'.
description: A sinister hidden master who communicates with his followers through a magic mirror, his face fading from it with a wicked smile after discovering a secret about Zane (Ep 739); when he projects a wisp of his soul, the Cobalt Dragon swallows it whole (Ep 759). He corresponds to the source's Heartless Master, who projects his soul through the Eight Trigrams Mirror, covets Luo Zheng's secrets, and dreams of making the entire Central Domain his fiefdom.

name: Star Field Divine Kingdom
reason: The source term 'Star Field Divine Kingdom' (also rendered 'Star Field Divine Nation') was carried over essentially verbatim.
description: One of the great Divine Kingdoms competing in the inter-kingdom martial gathering (Eps 799-871), led to the highest platform by its emperor with princes and princesses at the Life-and-Death and Spirit-Traverse tiers; it feels the heat of the contest most after failing to secure a single early victory. Scott is among its named warriors (Ep 871). Matches the source's Star Field Divine Kingdom of the four Divine Kingdoms arc.

name: Wind Divine Kingdom
reason: The source's 'Heavenly Wind Divine Kingdom' (also rendered 'Tianfeng Divine Nation') was shortened to 'Wind Divine Kingdom' for the adaptation.
description: One of the great Divine Kingdoms at the inter-kingdom gathering (Eps 803-895), whose scornful Crown Prince mutters 'A bunch of idiots' at the cheering crowd -- a line taken directly from the source's Crown Prince of the Heavenly Wind Divine Kingdom. Its royal line includes a princess outranking the average crown prince, and War King Wind of this kingdom holds a coveted treasure (Ep 831).

name: House Blackwood
reason: The source's 'Zhang Clan', owners of the famous Tianlu Auction House, was localized as the noble 'House Blackwood' to fit the show's Legacy House naming scheme.
description: A noble house that owns no land or armies but controls the financial arteries of the entire Empire (Eps 96-337), running The Gilded Gavel auction house and nurturing relationships with promising talents before anyone else recognizes them; members include Dustin, Corbin and Ingrid. Corresponds to the source's Zhang Clan, the merchant power behind the Tianlu Auction House whose disciples include Zhang Wuxian.

name: Henry
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Hao Shige' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Henry', a plain, solid name for a proud top disciple.
description: The top Outer Disciple of Misty Peak (Eps 80-229), wielder of the Azure Blade, whose best-in-class performance during the trials curdles into white-faced humiliation and plotted revenge once Zane eclipses him; he later freezes in terror when real monsters appear. He is the source's Hao Shige, the 'number one outer court disciple' whose composure and pride shatter after Luo Zheng kills a Demon Clan member he could not face.

name: Walsh
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Yan Jiu' was fully localized to the US surname-style name 'Walsh', suiting a cold professional assassin.
description: A Great Houses assassin at Nature Level rank 6 (Eps 148-150) who fights from inside a swirling black fog and speaks in a surprisingly high, thin voice despite being a man; Zane kills him by reading his dagger work. He corresponds to Yan Jiu, the black-fog wielder of the aligned source chapters (~135), whose fog is tied to his Quintessential Origin Energy.

name: Chase
reason: The source's master refiner 'Che Daozi' was localized to the near-homophone US name 'Chase', preserving the sound of the surname Che.
description: A legendary weaponsmith, already dead in the story's present (Eps 154-293), famed for works like the Green Wave; he died pouring the last of his life into an unfinished blade, leaving instructions that it be given to whoever could complete it as a Mythic Weapon -- the sword Zane finishes as the Streamer. He is the source's Che Daozi, who passed away mid-refinement of the incomplete Flowing Light Sword, entrusting his unfinished will to a 'fated person'.

name: Langdon
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhou Tong' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Langdon', fitting a brawny, reputation-proud competitor.
description: A Level Nine Adept from Azure Peak and Zane's first-round opponent in the All Peaks Competition (Eps 235-238), a fighter whose whole identity rests on his overwhelming strength and his twin 'Rolling Lightning Hammers'; he is left paralyzed with shock when Zane counters him. He is the source's Zhou Tong, born with divine strength, who pins opponents with his 'Swamp Trap' technique and crushes them with bronze hammers (chs 223-224).

name: Entrance Exam
reason: The source's two-stage entry process -- the preliminary 'sea examination' followed by the Blue Cloud Sect's own test -- was compressed into a single 'Entrance Exam' for the adaptation.
description: The qualifying examination recruits must pass to join the Skyreach Sect (Eps 28-55), demanding peak performance; rivals even paid four candidates to rough Zane up mid-exam, mirroring the source's hired killers at the sea examination (ch 19). Failed recruits are sent away immediately, and even the sect's lowest-ranked peaks measure prospective disciples against it.

name: Legendary Beast
reason: The source classification 'Mythological Beast' was renamed 'Legendary Beast' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A classification tier for powerful creatures such as the Cloud Leopard (Eps 282-1013), prized down to their blood and bones but still a rank below true divine beings; a 'Greater Legendary Beast' tier is also referenced. Localizes the source's 'Mythological Beast' classification, which likewise has 'Super Mythological Beasts' above it.

name: Core-Forged Realm
reason: The source cultivation stage 'Divine Core Realm' was renamed 'Core-Forged Realm' to fit the show's forging-themed terminology.
description: A major cultivation realm of the true-essence path (Eps 458-891) whose holders rank among the absolute elite; historically it was a huge deal for even a top disciple of a major sect to grasp a sliver of Law Power while still within it. Localizes the source's Divine Core Realm, which sits between the Divine Reflection Realm and the False Tribulation Realm.

name: Eddy
issues: Master sheet records him as 'Eddy Warrick', but the delivered episodes use only 'Eddy' (no 'Eddy Warrick' found in the corpus). The Warrick surname would collide with the unrelated House Warrick / Adrian Warrick; in the source he is Wei Yulong of the Drifting Cloud Sect, unconnected to either.
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Wei Yulong' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Eddy'; the master sheet's surname 'Warrick' does not appear in the delivered episodes.
description: Leader of the Crimson Sect (Grade Two, Heartlands) and an external steward for Cloud Hall who arrives with nine Soul Realm disciples (Eps 354-367); his commands are law to his disciples, who have learned harsh lessons for defying them, and he grows uncharacteristically cautious after gauging Finn's proven strength. He is the source's Wei Yulong, Sect Master of the Drifting Cloud Sect, who trusts his intuition about Luo Zheng's monstrous strength and forbids his ace disciple Huo Diting from challenging him (ch 344).

name: Adler
reason: The source character, identified only as a disciple surnamed 'Pang', was given the full US-style name 'Adler', a hard-edged name fitting an aggressive rival.
description: The condescending top disciple of the Duskfall Sect, a spear wielder who placed third in The Crimson Crucible and stays hostile toward Zane throughout the Sea of Raging Fire trials (Eps 361-364), refusing to take no for an answer and gasping in despair when Zane outperforms him. He corresponds to the source's disciple surnamed Pang, who sneered at Luo Zheng during the Scarlet Fire Snake trial and hoped to feed him to the beast to clear his own path (ch 349).

name: Arnold
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Feng Guanyu' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Arnold', a weighty classic name befitting a revered dead master.
description: A legendary rune master of the Ethereal Spirit Sect, long dead but still the benchmark of Heartlands runecraft (Eps 424-760); without access to ancient inheritances or divine textures, he figured everything out himself and created a rune with the power of a three-star divine texture. He is the source's Feng Guanyu, whose surviving runes are collected as treasures and whose 'perfect brush stroke' no one in the Central Domain has matched since his death.
